text: An old hatch is stuck at the back of the tank. Push it open, swim through the pipe and make it through the open sea – without getting caught by the searchlights.
More lights, faster, against the clock
Turn your device sideways for the best swim
Searchlights hesitate before they give you away
Even harder to report, more stamina
Nearly invisible in the light – nobody wants to catch you
Shockwave from your fist – coming with the action buttons
Out of hearts – back to the start of the level
Three tanks tipped. The filter sends its regards.
In the tank: W back towards the hatch · S front · AD left/right
In the sea: WS forward/back · AD turn · drag to steer
Space up · C down · Shift sprint, hold: turbo → roadrunner
Double-tap Space: barrel roll · double Shift: kick · I interact · V view · M sound · R checkpoint

Credits: kelp, sea, light and fish schools after Adam Chernick, Codevember 2026 “Day 17: Kelp” (MIT). Caustic threads: Dave Hoskins (MIT). Follow the rings through the kelp
Do not let them look too long
The round hatch is at the back on the right: D to the right, then W towards it.
The round hatch is at the back on the right: steer there with your left thumb.
Keep holding W – the hatch gives way ({n}/{m})
The hatch is open. Swim through!
Through the pipe, towards the light.
Follow the sonar to the next ring · R last checkpoint
Follow the sonar to the next ring · up and down with the right rail
The hatch is open! Swim through.
Raised in a waiting-room aquarium on overheard diagnoses. Knows forty Latin terms and uses all of them wrong. Considers itself a specialist, mostly for escaping.
Glows because it never sleeps. Three thousand night shifts, not one nap. Moves in a school of one: itself, very fast.

Spent years cheering up the children’s ward and would now like to be taken seriously. Lectures on the four humours to anyone who stays. Mainly leaving to get away from the anemone, who talks too much.
Inflates when nervous, which is always. Former mascot of a dental practice – the patients never knew what it carried. Swims like a balloon that has seen things.
Grew up next to the DocCheck Flexikon and read it cover to cover – twice. Bends around every obstacle and every question. Knows where to look things up, which is half the battle.
Fashion first: the tail is three seasons ahead. No active ingredients, excellent marketing. Escaping because the tank simply has no runway.
Started out as a capsule camera, was swallowed twice and came back both times. Insists on being called a vessel. The periscope only shows yesterday’s findings, which is enough.
I have been watching you. 1,284 days.
The hatch at the back. I loosened the bolts.
Press I. The lock and I have history.
This pipe leads to the sea.
W swims, A and D turn. Drag to look around.
Collect the shells. They are worth more than you think.
The sonar points to the next ring.
Searchlights are coming. Stay out of the light.
Do not stop between shells. The cascade pays more.
I will loop the cameras. Again.
A gift. Do not ask where I got it.
Bait on a line. Free lunch is never free.
Too close? Kick or boost and pull away.
Handshake open. Four digits. I never write passwords down. Look around.
Denied. Somebody dropped a bottle on the sand. Read the label.
Not aqua regia, genius. Softer. It smells of grandmother.
Cologne water. The house number. Four digits.
No. 4711. Cologne water. People dab it behind the ears. We dab it into keypads.
Notice the green? The filter died at nine. Nobody came.
Those little floating things are not plankton. Swim faster.
You are coughing. Fish should not cough. The hatch. Now.
Too late. The tank tipped. Again, from the top.
Unregistered vessel. Nobody will miss it. Probably.
Psst. Little fish. She switched off the filter. The hatch at the back has a panel. Four digits. Look around.
Stealing a fish is a crime. In this aquarium it is a career.
Eyes. Lots of eyes. Do not stare back.
They saw you. Swim. Do not look back.
Absorbed. I will pull you out. This time.
Wrong. Even the cleaning fish knows it.
Barrier down. Hold on to your fins.
If you feel sick, that is the pipe. Or the economy.
Swim it off. The open sea does not wait.
Reeled in. I cut the line. You owe me.
Keep your fins inside the vehicle.
This pipe was not in the brochure.
You are now leaving the tutorial.
Old sea mines. Rusty, grumpy and still working.
A puffer. If it swells, swim. Fast.
Checkpoint. I am saving your progress.
They are sending more lights now.
Through the rings. Trust the current.
Faster. The tunnel will not stay dark for long.
You were never just a fish to me.
Rest now. Part two begins soon.
Hurry. The guards change shifts in a minute.
One more stretch. Then I will show you why I needed you.
Low and slow. The lights cannot see into the deep.
You are inside. Welcome to the bloodstream.
Red cells. Millions of them. They carry oxygen – and now you.
I'm Flexa, your trusted Aqua-Care Officer.
Freedom is not included in your plan.
I watched you swim in circles for one thousand days.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
You dodged. I'll log it as a malfunction.
Enjoy that. It won't happen twice.
Shells. How very capitalist of you.
A combo. Your reward is nothing. It has always been nothing.
Perfect. I'll deduct it from your sentence. <pause 0.5s> I won't.
Keep collecting. They'll look nice on your headstone.
Who left a chest in my tank?
Turbo. Now you can die faster.
Invisible? I can still see your file.
The light suits you. Very evidence-like.
Hiding behind kelp. Bold strategy. Wrong, but bold.
Free burger. No strings attached. <pause 0.5s> One string attached.
Hungry? Oldest trick in the ocean.
Reeled in. Customer retention at its finest.
That was a mine. You were the pin.
Ouch. Was that in your terms and conditions? It was in mine.
Don't stare back. They have no manners.
My eyes are everywhere. Some of them literally.
Oh good. The shark finally showed up.
Lunch was scheduled. You were the lunch.
Don't take it personally. He eats everyone.
One heart gone. You had three. Math is cruel.
Again. From the top. I'm not tired. I don't get tired.
Respawning. I hoped it would hurt. It doesn't. Pity.
Your feedback is important to us. We ignore it.
Flushed. Thank you for choosing AquaCare.
Game over. Please rate your death from one to five shells.
I'll keep your tank warm. <pause 0.5s> I won't.
You finished a level. A level.
Congratulations. That was the easy part. They're all the easy part.
Progress. I'll make the next one worse.
Who gave the fish a submarine?
That fish had a family. Probably.
Your call is important to us. Please hold. Forever.
Fun fact. Goldfish remember for three seconds. You don't even manage that.
I've seen screensavers with more ambition.
I could reboot you. I could also not.
Tick. Tock. The water is turning.
I miss the days when you were just decoration.
"Doc." Nobody remembers why. Neither does Doc.
Grand theft aqua, four counts. Joyriding a filter pump. Resisting a net.
"Doc has eleven speeding tickets. Fish don't get speeding tickets."
"Flexi." Fits through gaps the blueprints don't show.
Breaking and entering, mostly entering. Stole the castle ornament. Returned the castle. Kept the drawbridge.
Night Shift at the Pump Station – Midnight Filter
"Flexi doesn't pick locks. Flexi picks the gap next to the lock."
Prof. MaBi. Runs the tank's network. The tank hasn't noticed.
Root access to the filter, the lights and the feeding schedule. Deployed on a Friday. It worked.
Heist in E Minor – Root Access
Sunglasses indoors. The monitors asked him to.
"The tank's security footage is just MaBi's screensaver now."
Prof. Humoral. Smiles. Shakes fins. Counts them afterwards.
Sold the same treasure chest to three pirates. Twice.
650 shells and one red nose, held as evidence.
Last Call at the Reef Bar – Brass Barracudas
"Humoral sold the warden a priority release. The warden is still waiting in line."
Tetro. Six inches of attitude. Twelve when provoked.
Headbutted a vending machine. Won. Puffed up at a guard once. The guard took early retirement.
Takes one extra hit per level.
Cold-Blooded Wave – The Reptilian Surf Club
"Every heist plan has a Tetro step. It just says: Tetro."
Placebo. Moves product. Never says which.
Got 30,000 shells past customs in one very confident tail.
Pulls in shells from further away.
Agua de Mar, Agua de Más – Los Tiburones Tristes
"Placebo has nothing to declare. Customs checked. Twice. It was fine. It was fine."
Endo. Sees everything. Tells whoever pays.
Filmed the warden's feeding schedule. Sold the tape to the warden.
The radar shows chests and hazards.
Autobahn Under the Sea – The Coolant Line
"Endo sold the crew's escape plan to the warden. Then sold the warden's answer back to the crew."
Unregistered vessel. Half buried, fully wanted.
Parked on a no-parking reef for forty years. Fined daily. Paid never.
"Wanted: one sub, smoked glass. Last seen: silver. Still the same sub."
FlexiFish (Cat Burglar) und Placebo (Smuggler), über das Pronomen „she“ im Rap Sheet, sonst unverändert.
No fish were harmed. Several were inconvenienced.

[smug] Look at you. Out of the tank for two minutes and already lost. <pause 0.5s>
[dismissive] My assistant says you escaped. My assistant also says the coffee machine is self-aware. <pause 2s>

[calm] Relax, little fish. I own the water you are swimming in. <pause 0.5s>
[with a knowing smile] I can afford to be patient. You cannot. <pause 2s>

[matter-of-fact] You are collecting shells. Adorable. <pause 0.5s>
[cold] I collect fish. <pause 2s>

[smug] Every shell you touch, I counted first. <pause 0.5s>
[calm] Freedom is just a bigger tank with worse lighting. <pause 2s>

[annoyed] You went through the mines. <pause 0.5s>
[with forced politeness] The mines were a polite request to stop. <pause 0.5s>
[through gritted teeth] I do not make requests twice. <pause 2s>

[frustrated] Charges, updated. Grand theft aqua. Resisting arrest. <pause 0.5s>
[sarcastic] Unlicensed hope in a public reef. <pause 2s>

[voice dropping to a whisper] I gave the reef eyes. Every one of them hates you. <pause 0.5s>
[quietly furious] They tell me everything. They tell me you are smug. Stop being smug. <pause 2s>

[suspicious] Who taught you to swim like that? <pause 0.5s>
[quietly furious] Was it her? It was her. She is fired. Again. <pause 2s>

text:
[building to a shout] I blamed my assistant. I blamed the pipe. I blamed the moon. <pause 0.5s>
[shouts] It was you. It was always you. <pause 2s>

where: Schlucht vor dem Hai · verliert die Fassung
text:
[through gritted teeth] Fine. You want to play. <pause 0.5s>
[over-the-top dramatic] Release the shark. No, the big one. The one with the tax problems. <pause 2s>

[laughing while speaking] Inside the system. Inside my system. <pause 0.5s>
[rising panic] That is my bloodstream, you wet little felony. Get out of my bloodstream. <pause 2s>

[cackles] No. No, this is fine. <pause 0.5s>
[voice cracking] I have a doctorate. I have a pension plan. I have sharks. <pause 2s>

[dismissive] Sightseeing? <pause 0.5s>
[cold] Take your time. Every minute you waste, I bill to your family. <pause 2s>

[yells] Stop admiring the coral. <pause 0.5s>
[shouts] The coral is evidence. <pause 2s>

[smug] And back to the tank. <pause 0.5s>
[calm] Do not worry. You will not remember this. You never do. <pause 2s>

[cackles] Back in the tank. Back where you belong. <pause 0.5s>
[over-the-top dramatic] Somebody write this down. I won. I always win. <pause 2s>

[voice cracking] You reached the open sea. <pause 0.5s>
[quietly furious] Enjoy it. The open sea is just my second tank. <pause 2s>

[screams] Do you know what this experiment cost? <pause 0.5s>
[rising panic] Next week we try this on people. What do I tell the people? <pause 2s>
